mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% signals a tightening monetary policy regime that raises discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5%, or the average return in triggered periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate below 4.5% signals tightening labor market conditions that increase wage pressures and inflation expectations, prompting the Fed to maintain restrictive policy and suppressing equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX generates positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases when UNRATE falls below 4.5%, or the mean return in such periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts above 1.3 million units signals strong consumer demand and confidence, which drives corporate revenues and earnings expectations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances when HOUST exceeds 1.3 million, or the average return in high-housing periods is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in industrial production below 110 index points signals weakening manufacturing activity and deteriorating economic momentum, which increases recession risk and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX generates positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases when INDPRO falls below 110, or the average return in such periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS signal a persistent inflationary environment that triggers aggressive monetary tightening, increasing real rates and reducing equity risk appetite, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where both CPIAUCSL exceeds 207.5 and FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5%, or the joint signal fails to produce a statistically significant negative return (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in PAYEMS and decline in UNRATE signals strong labor market tightening, which increases wage pressures and inflation expectations, prompting the Fed to maintain restrictive policy and suppressing equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 100k and UNRATE decreases > 0.2pp in 3 months
failure_condition: SPX generates positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where PAYEMS rises >100k and UNRATE falls >0.2pp, or the joint signal does not produce a significantly negative return (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) above 380 billion dollars signals strong consumer demand, which boosts corporate revenues and earnings growth expectations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances when RSAFS exceeds 380 billion, or the average return in high-demand periods is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in industrial production below 110 index points combined with a rise in the unemployment rate above 4.7% signals a dual shock of weakening manufacturing and labor market deterioration, increasing recession risk and leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX generates positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where INDPRO < 110 and UNRATE > 4.7%, or the joint signal fails to produce a significantly negative return (t-test p > 0.05).
